$comment: What performs each screen's primary action in VLD-UX-DRAUPNIR-001 section 8. RF-27. Read by tests/unit/test_screen_inventory.py, which fails if a screen, its action text, or an operation named here drifts from the UX specification or from docs/api/openapi.json. Three kinds: an operation that performs the action; navigation, where the action opens a view and names the read that view uses; and readOnly, where the screen performs no action in this release and says why. A readOnly entry for a screen whose section 8 row still names an action cites the amendment proposing the row change.

S01.action: Navigate to the thing that needs attention
S01.reason: The overview links to the run or gate that needs attention; following a link performs nothing, and the views it opens read the run board and the approval queue.

S02.reason: Opening a corpus moves to its sources in the licence register; nothing is changed by opening it.

S05.reason: A curated corpus is ingested into HODD and sealed at its address, so curating the same jurisdiction again is refused by the store rather than overwriting it. A different curation is a new corpus with its own address and lineage. A single stage is not re-run on its own because decontamination against the evaluation sets cannot be skipped.

S13.reason: Opening a model moves from the registry to that model's artefacts and evidence; nothing is changed by opening it.

S14.reason: Opening the lineage moves from a model to its chain back to base licences and corpus hashes; nothing is changed by opening it.

S18.reason: Reviewing moves from the queue to one artefact's evidence and decision, where the decision itself is S19's action.

S22.reason: A site is registered in MEGINGJORD when it is commissioned, together with deploying the core and issuing its certificates (SAD 10.2 and 11A.1). A forge that registered sites from its own console would be a second site registry that the federation does not hold.

S23.reason: Plug-ins install into the API environment as signed distributions and are verified at first load (SAD 11.1), and the installed set cannot change without a restart. Enabling one is a signed, deploy-time step rather than a switch in the console.

S24.reason: A policy change is a GLEIPNIR configuration change that is file based and version controlled (SAD 5.2 and 11.1), distributed by MEGINGJORD and pulled by each forge (SAD 11A.1). A forge that published versions itself would diverge from the version the federation distributes.

S25.reason: Roles are assigned in the identity provider and arrive in the token's roles or groups claim, with MEGINGJORD the RBAC source of truth (SAD 11A.1). A role assigned in the console would be a grant the identity provider knows nothing about.

S27.reason: Copying an entry puts the entry the screen already read onto the clipboard, in the browser; there is nothing for the API to perform.

S30.reason: The CON-A local view reads the appliance it is attached to and has no API dependency at all (Decision U2), so it survives the network failure it exists for.

S31.reason: The CON-B panel is a kiosk nobody stands at, so it has no navigation, no site switcher and no control of any kind.
